name: Dark Teal Grey
lede: Dark Teal Grey is a muted, blue-green grey named for teal, the dabbling duck, and recorded in both Ridgway's 1912 plates and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955.

sections.title: A duck's name, dulled
sections.body:
Our data files this as a plant-and-landscape word, tracing "teal" to the duck rather than to a pigment or dye [1]. Both Ridgway's 1912 atlas and the ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 carry it, though our source note does not keep the specific plate or block number for this exact entry [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 36, chroma 11, hue 215 degrees: dark, only lightly saturated, and sitting between blue and green [1].

Its nearest distinct neighbor by computed color distance is [[dark-delft-blue|Dark Delft Blue]], 3.0 units away and read in our data as "almost the same" [2]. One step further sits [[blue-ochre|Blue Ochre]], 3.4 units off and called "bluer" [2]. Its parent family word is [[dark-teal]], the lighter, more saturated color this grey is a muted version of [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 143, as photographed, more common than 65 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.7 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [3]. Pierre-Auguste Renoir is its most devoted painter here, with the color present in 5 of 50 of his works in the archive, well above the baseline of the museums those works come from [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color, in 43 percent of its matches, by lightness rank within the canvas [3].
